title: Quantum Motion from Local Transition Susceptibility
abstract: We characterize quantum motion based on the susceptibility of a quantum state to weak local state conversion. The inverse susceptibility can be interpreted as a passage speed characterizing local motion independently of probability transport. For individual WKB branches, it reproduces the magnitude of the local dispersion velocity in both propagating and evanescent regions. A relativistic extension yields a passage speed bounded by the speed of light, reaching this bound at the finite energy corresponding to the center of the mass gap, where the evanescent decay length equals the reduced Compton wavelength. This identifies the reduced Compton wavelength as the shortest stationary evanescent length scale compatible with relativistic quantum motion.
summary: The paper introduces the concept of passage speed derived from the transition susceptibility, offering a method to characterize quantum motion independent of net probability flow. By applying this technique to relativistic systems, the authors show that this passage speed correctly predicts local dispersion velocities and establishes the reduced Compton wavelength as a fundamental length scale governing relativistic quantum dynamics.
main_problem: To characterize quantum motion independently of probability transport by analyzing how a quantum state responds to weak local perturbations.
main_result: The inverse transition susceptibility defines a passage speed that reproduces the local dispersion velocity in both propagating and evanescent regions, establishing a relativistic bound related to the reduced Compton wavelength.
method: The methodology involves calculating the transition susceptibility ($\chi$) of quantum states subjected to weak localized couplings ($J$), defining the passage speed as $v_p = \chi^{-1}$.
model_or_system: The analysis considers general quantum states, extending from non-relativistic Schrödinger equations to relativistic Klein-Gordon waveguides coupled transversely. The system is probed by applying weak local perturbations.
key_observables: Passage speed ($v_p$), transition susceptibility ($\chi$), and the local dispersion velocity.
important_parameters: The coupling strength ($J$), energy ($\epsilon$), wave number ($k$), decay constant ($\kappa$), and the reduced Compton wavelength ($\lambda_C/c$).
main_assumptions: For relativistic extensions, an auxiliary two-stream model is introduced for evanescent states. The definition of $v_p$ depends on the placement of the coupling evaluation window.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the general coupling scheme; Figure 2 shows the ratio $v_p/v$ for a standing wave at various coupling positions ($x_c$). Figure 3 plots $v_p/c$ versus the Lorentz factor ($\gamma$) for both propagating and evanescent regimes.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the concept of passage speed via susceptibility in general settings (including standing waves). It then extends this framework to a relativistic model involving coupled Klein-Gordon waveguides, deriving specific formulas for $v_p$ in both propagating and decaying regimes.
why_interesting: This work provides a novel diagnostic tool ($v_p$) to measure intrinsic quantum motion that is robust even when standard probability current measures vanish (e.g., standing waves), linking it directly to fundamental scales like the Compton wavelength.

figures.caption: Figure 1. Coupling scheme defining the local transition sus- ceptibility. A weak coupling of rate J acts over the region C of length L, transferring amplitude from the initial channel |1⟩to the orthogonal channel |2⟩. The populations N1 and N2 are integrated over the same downstream comparison region R. Their ratio in the weak-coupling limit defines χ(L, xc) and the passage speed vp(L, xc) = χ−1(L, xc).

Figure 2. Finite-window passage speed for the standing wave formed by reflection at a hard wall, Eq. (7), shown for three positions xc of the coupling region. The response depends on kL and on the standing-wave phase 2kxc because the two counterpropagating branches interfere within the coupling re- gion. For kL ≫1, this interference averages out and vp(L, xc) approaches the single-branch speed v = ℏk/m. The vertical range is truncated at vp/v = 4.
